MENDEL'S OF INHERITANCE
Law of Dominance: This law states that in a hybrid, the dominant allele expresses itself while the recessive
allele is suppressed.
Law of Segregation: It states that the two alleles for a character segregate or separate during gamete
formation.
Law of Independent Accortment: This law explains that the factors for different pairs of contrasting
characters behave independently of each other during gamete formation.
SOME BASIC TERMS RELATED TO GENETICS
• Monohybrid Croce: This refers to a genetic cross involving a single trait with two alleles. Typically, in a
classic Mendelian monohybrid cross, the phenotype ratio is 2:1 (dominant to recessive traits) and the
genotype ratio is 1:2:1 (homozygous dominant, heterozygous, homozygous recessive).
• Dihybrid Cron: A dihybrid cross involves two pairs of different traits, each with two alleles. The phenotype
ratio is usually in a Mendelian dihybrid cross.

• Meterozygouc: An individual having two different alleles for a specific gene (e.g, Aa).
• Homozygous: An individual having two identical alleles for a particular gene (e.g„ AA or aa).
• Allele: One of two or more alternative forms of a gene, result in different traits, even though they are for
the same gene.
• Dominant: An allele is dominant if it is expressed in the phenotype of an organism that has only one copy
of that allele.
• Recessive: An allele is recessive if it is expressed in the phenotype only when two copies are present (i.e„
not expressed when a dominant allele is present).
• Phenotype: The set of observable characteristics Of an organism resulting from the interaction of its
genotype with the environment.
• Genotype: The genetic constitution Of an organism, determining its specific traits.

MUTATION
A change in the DNA sequence of an organism's genome.
• Can occur due to various factors such as errors during DNA replication, exposure to certain chemicals or
radiation, and can result in genetic diversity.
• Mutations can be beneficial, harmful, or neutral in their effects on the organism
• They play a crucial role in evolution by introducing new genetic variations, and can also be the cause of
certain genetic disorders or diseases.

RENAL
Renal dialysis is a device to treat ki ney failure. This
process uses an artificial kidney (hemodialyser) to
remove waste and extra fluid from the blood. The
blood is taken out from the body and filtered by
this artificial kidney and than reintroduced into the
body using a dialysis machine. Dialysis can be
categorised into three primary types: in-center
hemodialysis, home hemodialysis, and peritoneal
dialysis.
